Date: 2026-05-14

## 3. Major Financial AI Company News

**Anthropic and Gates Foundation launch $200M AI public-goods partnership**  
Date: 2026-05-14  
Link: https://www.anthropic.com/news/gates-foundation-partnership  
Summary: Anthropic and the Gates Foundation committed $200 million over four years in grant funding, Claude credits, and technical support for AI work in global health, life sciences, education, agriculture, and economic mobility. Anthropic says outputs may include datasets, benchmarks, connectors, and evaluation frameworks released as public goods.  
Why it matters: This expands frontier-lab involvement in public-sector AI deployment and creates a sizable subsidized channel for Claude adoption in development and science domains.

**Wirestock raises $23M to supply multimodal data to AI labs**  
Date: 2026-05-14  
Link: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/14/wirestock-raises-23m-to-supply-multi-modal-data-to-ai-labs/  
Summary: Wirestock raised a $23 million Series A led by Nava Ventures to expand its business supplying licensed images, video, design assets, gaming content, and 3D data to foundation-model developers.  
Why it matters: The funding reflects continuing demand for rights-cleared multimodal data as labs push beyond text and face tighter scrutiny over training provenance.

## 5. Regulation & Policy

**OpenAI backs idea of global AI governance body including U.S. and China**  
Date: 2026-05-13  
Link: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-13/openai-floats-idea-of-global-ai-governance-body-with-us-china  
Summary: Bloomberg reported that OpenAI would support a U.S.-led global AI governance body that includes China, citing OpenAI VP of Global Affairs Chris Lehane.  
Why it matters: The position signals that major labs are moving from domestic safety frameworks toward international governance proposals, especially around advanced-model resilience and cross-border risk management.

**AI becomes a visible U.S. midterm-election issue**  
Date: 2026-05-13  
Link: https://www.semafor.com/article/05/13/2026/ai-assumes-larger-role-in-us-elections  
Summary: Semafor reported that AI policy, data-center opposition, donor activity, and regulation debates are surfacing in U.S. midterm campaigns, including a New York congressional primary framed partly around AI regulation.  
Why it matters: AI politics are shifting from federal expert circles into local electoral conflict, especially where data centers, energy demand, jobs, and platform regulation intersect.

**AI chatbots misdirect users to real personal phone numbers**  
Date: 2026-05-13  
Link: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/05/13/1137203/ai-chatbots-are-giving-out-peoples-real-phone-numbers/  
Summary: MIT Technology Review reported cases where generative AI systems surfaced private individuals’ phone numbers as if they belonged to businesses or service providers.  
Why it matters: This is a concrete consumer-harm pattern for AI search and answer systems: hallucinated or misattributed contact data can create privacy, harassment, and liability exposure.
